front_blocks.md: Define **saturated hydrocarbon**.

back_blocks.md: A **saturated hydrocarbon** is a compound of carbon and hydrogen that contains only carbon-carbon **single bonds** and no **double bonds**.

front_blocks.md: Why are alkanes described as saturated hydrocarbons?

back_blocks.md: **Alkanes** are described as **saturated** because they contain only carbon-carbon **single bonds** — there are no double bonds in their structure.

front_blocks.md: **True or False?**
The molecular formula of methane is CH<sub>4</sub>.

back_blocks.md: **True.**
**Methane** is the first member of the alkane homologous series and has the molecular formula CH<sub>4</sub>, fitting the general formula C<sub>n</sub>H<sub>2n+2</sub> with n = 1.

front_blocks.md: Define **homologous series**.

back_blocks.md: A **homologous series** is a family of compounds that share the same **general formula**, differ by CH<sub>2</sub> between successive members and show a gradual trend in physical properties.

front_blocks.md: Name the first five alkanes in order of increasing carbon number.

1. **Methane** (CH<sub>4</sub>)

3. **Propane** (C<sub>3</sub>H<sub>8</sub>)
4. **Butane** (C<sub>4</sub>H<sub>10</sub>)
5. **Pentane** (C<sub>5</sub>H<sub>12</sub>)

front_blocks.md: **True or False?**
Alkanes are generally very reactive compounds.

back_blocks.md: **False.**

**Alkanes** are generally **unreactive** compounds, though they do undergo combustion, can be cracked into smaller molecules and can react with **halogens** in the presence of **ultraviolet (UV) light**.

front_blocks.md: What condition is required for alkanes to react with halogens?

back_blocks.md: Alkanes react with halogens only in the presence of **ultraviolet (UV) radiation**, which provides the energy needed to initiate the **substitution reaction**.

front_blocks.md: Define **substitution reaction**.

back_blocks.md: A **substitution reaction** is a reaction in which one atom or group of atoms is swapped for another atom or group.

cards.back_md: A **substitution reaction** is a reaction in which one atom or group of atoms is swapped for another atom or group.

front_blocks.md: **True or False?**
Methane reacts with bromine in UV radiation to form bromomethane and hydrogen bromide.

back_blocks.md: **True.**
In the presence of **UV radiation**, **methane** undergoes a **substitution reaction** with **bromine**: CH<sub>4</sub> + Br<sub>2</sub> → CH<sub>3</sub>Br + **HBr**.

front_blocks.md: Methane reacts with chlorine in UV radiation to form **..........** and **..........** .

back_blocks.md: Methane reacts with chlorine in UV radiation to form **chloromethane** and **hydrogen chloride** (HCl).

front_blocks.md: What type of organic compound forms when an alkane reacts with a halogen?

back_blocks.md: A **halogenoalkane** (also called a haloalkane) forms, in which one hydrogen atom in the alkane has been replaced by a **halogen** atom.

cards.back_md: A **halogenoalkane** (also called a haloalkane) forms, in which one hydrogen atom in the alkane has been replaced by a **halogen** atom.

front_blocks.md: **True or False?**
Alkanes react with halogens in the dark without any energy input.

back_blocks.md: **False.**
The reaction between **alkanes** and **halogens** requires **ultraviolet (UV) radiation** to proceed — it does not occur in the dark.

front_blocks.md: What by-product is produced when methane reacts with chlorine in UV radiation?

back_blocks.md: **Hydrogen chloride** (HCl) is produced as a by-product alongside **chloromethane** (CH<sub>3</sub>Cl) in the reaction.
